title: t004: SharedWorker runtime mode for WebLLM connector
body:
## Summary

Replace the dedicated `Tools → WebLLM Worker` tab with an auto-injected SharedWorker so the LLM survives page navigation and is invisible/zero-config for users. After install + activate, AI tools should "just work": first AI request triggers a start modal, model loads, a small floating icon shows status across all subsequent admin (and optionally front-end) pages, and the model stays loaded as long as any tab on the install is open.

## Why now

- Current dedicated worker tab requires the user to manually navigate to `Tools → WebLLM Worker`, click "Load model", and keep that tab open. Users forget to do this and AI features 503.
- Chrome 124+ ships WebGPU support in both ServiceWorker and **SharedWorker** global scopes. SharedWorker is the better fit for cross-page persistence in a multi-page app like wp-admin (no browser-managed kill on idle, no keep-alive ping needed, naturally one-per-origin).
- The official `mlc-ai/web-llm-chat` uses ServiceWorker, but only because it's an SPA — they don't have our multi-page navigation problem. They also have a 5-second keep-alive ping fighting Chrome's idle-kill, which we'd avoid entirely with SharedWorker.

## Scope

~30h across 8 phases:

1. Spike on AI Client SDK editor integration hooks (~2h)
2. SharedWorker handler + MLCEngine wrapper (~5h, ~200 LOC, ~150 of which is custom because `@mlc-ai/web-llm` does not ship `SharedWorkerMLCEngine`)
3. Floating widget UI + state machine (~7h, ~400 LOC)
4. Bootstrap, injector, capability detection (~3h)
5. Settings + connector card UI update (~3h)
6. Editor middleware integration (apiFetch hook) (~5h)
7. Cross-browser testing + dedicated-tab fallback verification (~4h)
8. Docs, .distignore, readme updates (~2h)

## Key constraints

- Existing PHP REST broker (`inc/rest-api.php`, `Job_Queue`) **stays unchanged** — only the consumer changes.
- Existing dedicated-tab worker page **stays as fallback** for non-Chrome / older-Chrome users.
- All existing settings, options, REST routes, and bearer-token auth preserved.
- No streaming (same limitation as today).
- `@mlc-ai/web-llm` has NO `SharedWorkerMLCEngine` — must build a thin handler ourselves modelled on `WebWorkerMLCEngineHandler`.

## Open design decisions (deferred to PRD)

- apiFetch interception strategy: soft (poll status) vs better (intercept apiFetch) vs hybrid (intercept known endpoints, fall back to soft for unknown plugins)
- Auto-start vs on-demand model load default
- SharedWorker URL stability strategy (cache busting trade-off)
- Whether to inject the floating widget on the front-end by default or admin-only

## Tracking

- Plan: `todo/PLANS.md` (p001)
- PRD: `todo/tasks/prd-shared-worker-runtime.md`
- TODO: `TODO.md` (t004)

title: t005: Hook WebLLM into wpai_preferred_text_models filter so AI Experiments routes to the browser provider
body:
## What

Add a single `wpai_preferred_text_models` filter callback in `ultimate-ai-connector-webllm.php` that prepends the currently-configured WebLLM model to the list of preferred text generation models used by `WordPress/ai` and other consumers.

## Why

Discovered during the Phase 1 spike for #4 (see [spike-shared-worker-apifetch.md](https://github.com/Ultimate-Multisite/ultimate-ai-connector-webllm/blob/main/todo/tasks/spike-shared-worker-apifetch.md), finding F1):

1. The `WordPress/ai` plugin's `get_preferred_models_for_text_generation()` in `includes/helpers.php:142-176` returns a hardcoded list of Anthropic/Google/OpenAI models, then applies the `wpai_preferred_text_models` filter.
2. Our plugin does not hook into that filter.
3. Consequence: even with this plugin installed, activated, and a worker tab actively serving a loaded model, AI Experiments' excerpt generator (and every other consumer of `get_preferred_models_for_text_generation()`) routes to the commercial providers and never reaches WebLLM.

This is a correctness bug in the current architecture. It's independent of the SharedWorker rewrite (#4) but blocks any realistic testing of WebLLM-routed features. Fixing it now means #4's eventual testing has a real AI path to exercise.

## How

### Files to modify

**EDIT:** `ultimate-ai-connector-webllm.php` — add one `add_filter` call inside the existing namespace block, after the hook registrations on lines 52-56. The new hook is safe to register unconditionally (the filter target is from the `WordPress/ai` plugin, not the WP AI Client SDK, so it has no dependency on `class_exists` guards).

### Reference pattern

Model on the existing `add_filter` call on line 56 of `ultimate-ai-connector-webllm.php`:

```php
add_filter( 'http_request_args', __NAMESPACE__ . '\\extend_loopback_timeout', 10, 2 );
```

Same style (top-level `add_filter` in namespace, no backslash on the function name). The only difference is the callback is an anonymous closure instead of a named function reference.

### Exact code to insert

Add this block between lines 56 and 58 (after the `http_request_args` filter, before the `admin_menu` action):

```php
/**
 * Register WebLLM as a preferred text-generation provider so that consumers
 * of `wpai_preferred_text_models` (e.g. the WordPress/ai plugin's AI Experiments
 * features) route requests to the browser-side engine.
 *
 * Only prepended when a default model is configured — an empty model setting
 * leaves the preference list untouched so other providers remain usable.
 *
 * @param array<int, array{0: string, 1: string}> $preferred_models The existing preference list.
 * @return array<int, array{0: string, 1: string}>
 */
add_filter(
    'wpai_preferred_text_models',
    static function ( array $preferred_models ): array {
        $active = (string) get_option( 'webllm_default_model', '' );
        if ( '' === $active ) {
            return $preferred_models;
        }

        array_unshift( $preferred_models, array( 'ultimate-ai-connector-webllm', $active ) );
        return $preferred_models;
    },
    5
);
```

**Priority 5** (not the default 10) ensures we win against any other plugin hooking the same filter at default priority. WordPress's AI Experiments does not hook the filter itself, so priority 5 just means "early" without conflict.

### Gotchas

1. **Empty model option.** When `webllm_default_model` is empty, we leave the list alone. Otherwise the worker has no model to load and we'd be pointing consumers at a dead endpoint.
2. **Namespace.** The file uses `namespace UltimateAiConnectorWebLlm;`. The `add_filter` call MUST be inside that namespace block to match the existing hook registration style. Don't add a `\add_filter(...)` with a leading backslash.
3. **No `use function` needed.** `add_filter` and `get_option` are WordPress globals; PHP falls back to the root namespace automatically when they're not found in the current namespace.
4. **Do NOT** modify `inc/class-provider.php`, `inc/class-model.php`, or any of the REST API files. This task only touches `ultimate-ai-connector-webllm.php`.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **The filter callback is registered** — `grep -n "wpai_preferred_text_models" ultimate-ai-connector-webllm.php` returns exactly one match (the new `add_filter` line).
2. **PHP lint passes** — `php -l ultimate-ai-connector-webllm.php` reports no errors.
3. **PHPUnit tests still pass** — `composer test` exits 0 (no regressions).
4. **Runtime behaviour**: when `webllm_default_model` is set to a valid model ID and `apply_filters( 'wpai_preferred_text_models', [] )` is called, the returned array's first element is `['ultimate-ai-connector-webllm', '<model id>']`. Optionally add a quick unit test at `tests/test-preferred-models-filter.php` but this is not required.
5. **No unrelated changes** — the diff touches only `ultimate-ai-connector-webllm.php` and (optionally) a new test file.

## Verification commands

```bash
php -l ultimate-ai-connector-webllm.php
composer test
git diff --stat   # should show only ultimate-ai-connector-webllm.php and optionally tests/
grep -n "wpai_preferred_text_models" ultimate-ai-connector-webllm.php
```

## Context

- **Discovered by:** Phase 1 spike of #4 (see [spike doc](https://github.com/Ultimate-Multisite/ultimate-ai-connector-webllm/blob/main/todo/tasks/spike-shared-worker-apifetch.md) section "Incidental findings" F1)
- **Upstream filter definition:** `WordPress/ai/includes/helpers.php:142-176` function `get_preferred_models_for_text_generation`
- **Our provider ID:** `ultimate-ai-connector-webllm` (defined at `inc/class-provider.php:68`)
- **Default model option key:** `webllm_default_model` (registered in `inc/settings.php`)
- **Brief:** [todo/tasks/t005-brief.md](https://github.com/Ultimate-Multisite/ultimate-ai-connector-webllm/blob/main/todo/tasks/t005-brief.md)

title: t010: Phase 6 — apiFetch middleware integration (Hybrid-narrow)
body:
## What

Implement the **Hybrid-narrow** apiFetch middleware strategy locked during the Phase 1 spike. The middleware intercepts requests that are likely to route to WebLLM, holds them if the SharedWorker is idle, shows the start modal via `window.webllmWidget.promptAndLoad()`, and releases them once the model is loaded. Rejects cleanly on user cancel.

## Why

This is what turns "user clicks AI tool → 503 error" into "user clicks AI tool → modal pops up → click Start → AI works". The defining UX improvement of #4.

## Phase

**Phase 6 of 8** for #4.

## Blocked by

#7 (Phase 3 — Floating widget). This task calls `window.webllmWidget.getStatus()` and `window.webllmWidget.promptAndLoad()`, which are defined by #7. NOT blocked by #8 or #9 — can run in parallel with those once #7 is done.

title: t011: Phase 7 — Cross-browser testing + dedicated-tab fallback verification
body:
## What

Manually verify the full #4 implementation across the browsers, GPUs, and multi-tab scenarios listed in the PRD. Produce `todo/tasks/t011-test-report.md` with one row per scenario (Pass/Fail/Skipped + notes). Capture any failures as follow-up issues.

## Why

Software that ships with "works on my machine" has no future. The SharedWorker runtime touches multiple Chromium APIs, WebGPU, IndexedDB, and cross-tab messaging. Bugs surface only on certain GPU/OS/browser combinations. A structured pre-merge test pass is the cheapest way to catch them.

## Phase

**Phase 7 of 8** for #4.

## IMPORTANT — this task is NOT auto-dispatched

Cross-browser testing requires physical hardware (integrated and discrete GPUs), multiple browser installs, and human judgement for UX regressions. title: t013: Commit t011 testing fixes — cache-busting, content normalisation, hardware ref
body:
## What

Three uncommitted bug fixes on \`main\` discovered during t011 cross-browser testing need to be committed and PRed:

1. **Cache-busting for SharedWorker/bundle URLs** (\`inc/widget-injector.php\`) — appends \`?v=VERSION\` to all bundle URLs so Chrome invalidates the SharedWorker cache on plugin upgrade. Without this, Chrome reuses the old worker script across rebuilds.

2. **Content-parts normalisation in SharedWorker** (\`src/shared-worker.js\`) — adds \`flattenContent()\` and \`normaliseRequest()\` helpers. WebLLM non-VLM models reject OpenAI content-parts arrays; the WP AI SDK always sends them. Mirrors the normalisation already in \`src/worker.jsx\`.

3. **Hardware ref fix in floating widget** (\`src/floating-widget.jsx\`) — adds \`hardwareRef\` to mirror \`hardware\` state so the \`needs-load\` subscribe callback always sees the latest GPU info (closure over state is frozen at subscribe time). Also prefers \`CFG.defaultModel\` over the SharedWorker autoPick heuristic on autoStart.

## Why

These fixes are currently uncommitted on \`main\` — they exist in the working tree but have no commit or PR. They were made during t011 manual testing and must be committed before t012 (docs/release) can proceed.

## How

**Files to modify:**
- EDIT: \`inc/widget-injector.php\` — already modified, just needs committing
- EDIT: \`src/shared-worker.js\` — already modified, just needs committing

## Problem

GitHub Actions is deprecating Node.js 20. Actions running on Node.js 20 will be forced to Node.js 24 starting **June 2, 2026**, and Node.js 20 will be removed from runners on **September 16, 2026**.

This repo's workflows use actions that still run on Node.js 20, producing deprecation warnings on every run.

## Required upgrades

| Current | Upgrade to |
|---------|------------|
| `actions/checkout@v4` | `actions/checkout@v6` |
| `actions/setup-node@v4` | `actions/setup-node@v6` |

| `softprops/action-gh-release@v2` | Keep `@v2` -- set `FORCE_JAVASCRIPT_ACTIONS_TO_NODE24=true` env var until upstream ships Node 24 support |

EDIT: `.github/workflows/*.yml` -- find-and-replace the action version tags per the table above.

For `softprops/action-gh-release`, add this env var to the workflow or job level until upstream releases a Node 24 version:

```yaml
env:
  FORCE_JAVASCRIPT_ACTIONS_TO_NODE24: true
```

After merging, trigger a workflow run and confirm no Node.js 20 deprecation warnings appear in the annotations.

title: Replace ReactDOM.render() with createRoot() for React 18 compatibility
body:
## Summary

`floating-widget.js` and `widget-bootstrap.js` call the legacy `ReactDOM.render()` API, which is removed in React 18 and logs a console warning on every page load where WordPress ships React 18:

```
Warning: ReactDOM.render is no longer supported in React 18. Use createRoot instead.
Until you switch to the new API, your app will behave as if it's running React 17.
```

## Stack trace

```
render @ react-dom.js?ver=18.3.1.1:29726
t @ floating-widget.js?v=1.0.2:1
(anonymous) @ floating-widget.js?v=1.0.2:1
(anonymous) @ floating-widget.js?v=1.0.2:1
i @ widget-bootstrap.js?ver=1.0.2:1
```

## Fix

Replace `ReactDOM.render(<App />, container)` with the React 18 API:

```js
import { createRoot } from 'react-dom/client';

const root = createRoot(container);
root.render(<App />);
```

WordPress has shipped React 18 since WP 6.6, so this affects all current installs.

title: Migrate WebLLM build and release tooling to pnpm
body:
## Goal

Migrate the WebLLM asset build, build-drift gate, release archive, and contributor guidance from npm to pnpm.

## Why this repository benefits

- The npm lockfile is nearly 23,000 lines and includes heavyweight WebLLM, Transformers, and WordPress build tooling.
- Pull requests and releases both perform clean Node installs.
- pnpm should substantially reduce repeated storage/install work while detecting undeclared transitive build dependencies.

## Implementation scope

- Pin pnpm and a supported Node range in `package.json`; replace `package-lock.json` with `pnpm-lock.yaml`.
- Migrate `.github/workflows/build-drift.yml` and `.github/workflows/release.yml` to frozen pnpm installs and pnpm caching.
- Update `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `.distignore`, and `composer.json` archive exclusions.
- Audit `webpack.config.js` for root-resolved Babel loader/preset/plugin packages and declare direct dependencies.
- Make build/archive sequencing explicit and remove or validate `$npm_package_name` assumptions.
- Preserve every generated JS, MJS, WASM, worker, and SharedWorker artifact and filename.
- Configure only required dependency build scripts.

## Acceptance criteria

- A clean frozen install and build leave committed `build/` assets unchanged.
- CI uses the exact pnpm version declared by the repository.
- The release ZIP excludes package-manager/development files and preserves runtime WebLLM assets.
- Browser smoke testing confirms worker and model assets load without module-resolution errors.

## Verification

```bash
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm run build -- --no-progress
git diff --exit-code -- build/
composer test
unzip -l ultimate-ai-connector-webllm.zip
git grep -nE '\b(npm ci|npm run|npx)\b' -- package.json .github AGENTS.md README.md
```
